thread:
Maya: heads up — noticed a regression in streamed responses after last night's kernel-selector tweak. p99 up ~5% for short-stream workloads (<=64 tokens). Anyone else seeing this?
Kevin: saw alerts. reproducing locally now with the stream simulator. looks like batches are getting formed but flushes happen early, starving larger batches.
Lina: hmm that sounds like our flush cadence heuristic kicking in when partial-decodes are active. can you paste a small profiler snapshot?
Kevin: sending small snippet from the profiler dump — relevant lines only:
```
[profiler] stream_handler: partial_decode_wait=12.4ms
[profiler] batch_builder: avg_wait=7.2ms, tail_wait=45.8ms
[profiler] kernel_selector: chosen_kernel=small_seq_opt_v2, score_delta=0.12
[profiler] kv_cache: hit_rate=0.82, miss_penalty=3.1ms
```
Maya: kernel_selector changed to prefer small_seq_opt_v2 in last deploy (it reduces token cost). Could that change interaction with continuous batching + streaming?
Oliver: yes — small_seq_opt_v2 has slightly higher per-seq overhead when context switch frequency is high (streaming partial decode does that). result: earlier flushes to keep latency, but reduced batching efficiency.
Lina: that matches. we tune flush cadence to target token_budget_per_batch=256, but partial-decode streams with early flush can reduce effective batch token budget to ~120. leads to more kernel invocations and backpressure spikes.
Maya: any quick mitigations? revert kernel selector? tweak flush policy?
Kevin: immediate mitigation: bump token_budget_per_batch target to 384 for streams and make queue policy prefer age+size rather than size-only. code change is tiny: toggle `StreamConfig.prefer_age=true` and `BatchConfig.token_budget=384` for stream routes.
Lina: also add a kludge: when partial-decode flag is set on a request, annotate as `streaming_eligibility=defer` so batcher lets it wait up to 25ms before forcing a flush. reduces partial-decode churn.
Oliver: we should validate CPU+GPU utilization impact — bigger batch target may increase latencies for first tokens. run A/B with canary weight 10%.
perf-bot: nightly-profile job finished: compare-to=baseline-19539, p99_stream_latency=+5.1%, avg_token_throughput=-3.0%, kv_miss_rate=+0.4%
Maya: thanks. Plan: 1) roll canary with prefer_age + token_budget bump for stream routes (10% traffic). 2) monitor p50/p95/p99 and kernel invocation counts. 3) if p99 improves but avg regresses too much, revert kernel_selector change and re-evaluate.
Kevin: dropping a quick filter query to gather kernel invocation histo across hosts:
```
select kernel_name, count(*) as invocations, avg(seq_len) from runtime_events
where route_type='stream' and ts > now() - interval '30 minutes'
group by kernel_name order by invocations desc;
```
Lina: I'll own the canary and dashboards. adding an alert: if stream p99 > baseline+3% for 5m, auto rollback.
Oliver: and I'll run microbench of small_seq_opt_v2 vs v1 with partial-decode enabled to understand the overhead.
Maya: awesome — thanks all. leaving notes in the deploy ticket. :thumbsup:
Kevin: one more note — KV cache staleness looked higher in the profiler; if we increase wait we might see slightly lower kv hit due to interleaving. watch kv_hit_rate on canary.
Lina: noted. will track kv_hit_rate and miss_penalty.
